samples.summary: useDocumentsPath cannot distinguish "workspaces still loading / failed" from "user has no workspaces", so an early Esc or back-button click lands on /documents instead of the document's workspace list
samples.evidence: `const { data: workspaces = [] } = useQuery(...)` then `const slug = workspaces.find(...)?.slug ?? workspaces[0]?.slug; return slug ? `/w/${slug}` : "/documents";`. While the `["workspaces"]` query is in flight (a hard refresh straight into /f/:id — FileDetail only gates on the `me`/`document` queries, not on workspaces) the hook returns "/documents". file-detail.tsx:131 captures that value in `close`, so pressing Esc or clicking "Back to documents" during that window navigates to the workspace-less list rather than /w/<slug>. The same happens permanently if fetchWorkspaces rejects. The hook exposes no loading/error state for callers to defer on, and none of the new tests cover the pending state (they all resolve the mock first).

samples.summary: Switching the keydown listener to window capture phase makes the viewer's Esc/arrow handling immune to stopPropagation, leaving only the DOM-selector heuristic as protection
samples.evidence: `window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey, true)` now runs before every descendant handler, so any current or future overlay/widget that shields itself by calling `e.stopPropagation()` on keydown (the previous bubble listener respected that) no longer suppresses navigation. Protection is now entirely `hasOpenOverlay()` (line 158), a hardcoded list of Radix markup shapes: a non-Radix portal panel (e.g. the createPortal popovers in app/docs/docs-link-popover.tsx:174, app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:177 pattern) or a native focus target that isn't INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable — e.g. a `<select>`, a Radix RadioGroup/Tabs strip — will see ArrowLeft/ArrowRight silently navigate the route away, and Esc leave the viewer, from under it. The guard is also DOM-shape coupled: if Radix changes `data-state`/`role`/`data-slot` attributes the guard silently stops guarding with no type or test failure.

samples.summary: The not-found redirect effect now depends on documentsPath, which changes when the workspaces query resolves — it can fire twice (duplicate "Document not found" toast + a second replace-navigate)
samples.evidence: `useEffect(() => { if (isDocumentError) { toast.error(...); navigate(documentsPath, {replace:true}); } }, [isDocumentError, navigate, documentsPath])`. If the document query errors before `fetchWorkspaces` resolves, documentsPath is "/documents"; when workspaces arrive it becomes "/w/<slug>" and, for as long as FileShell is still mounted (the redirect is async relative to React's commit, and placeholderData keeps the tree alive), the effect re-runs: a second toast and a second replace-navigate that can yank the user off a page they already moved to. The old code had the same shape with `fallbackSlug`, so this is a carried-over rather than introduced defect, but the new indirection makes the changing dependency less obvious.
